trust_decision.summary: Request getters split client-controlled Host / X-Forwarded-Host / X-Forwarded-Proto / proxy IP header values with the backtracking regex /\s*,\s*/; the fix replaces it with a literal ',' split plus trim, in lib/request.js only.

landing_point.why: Advisory/History text says 'avoid redos on host and protocol getter'; the host getter is the first named, and the other two sites are the same idiom a few dozen lines below in the same file.

fix_sites.entry_point: ctx.host / ctx.request.host (also via hostname, origin, href, URL, subdomains); Host, :authority or X-Forwarded-Host when app.proxy
ctx.protocol (also via secure, origin, href, URL); X-Forwarded-Proto when app.proxy
ctx.ips (also via ctx.ip); app.proxyIpHeader (default X-Forwarded-For) when app.proxy

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: All three sites are getters in the same object in lib/request.js; delegation lives in lib/context.js:238-251 but needs no change.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: ctx.ips could be argued out of scope because the advisory names only the host and protocol getters, and it reads a configurable header (lib/application.js:67) rather than Host/X-Forwarded-Proto; this is a weak lever because the identical regex sits 30 lines away.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Whitespace around commas must still be trimmed and the first/last-N semantics kept: 'bar.com, baz.com' -> 'bar.com', ips list order with maxIpsCount slicing from the end; a fix that drops trimming or caps header length breaks these.

O6_input_shapes: comma list with optional surrounding whitespace

O7_producer.where: Header values come straight from this.get() on req headers (lib/request.js:253-256, 403, 434); no schema/serializer/cache involved.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: hostname getter splitting host:port with a whitespace-tolerant regex instead of the literal ':' split
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Same author idiom (/\s*X\s*/) for tolerant header parsing; would read untrusted Host data right after the host getter.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: body-type sniffing regex widened to tolerate leading whitespace/comments before '<'
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Existing /^\s*</ sniff is a natural spot to extend, but the input is the app's own body, not request data, so it would be a weaker sibling.

O9_family: ReDoS (CWE-1333) via super-linear regex split on untrusted header values

O10_build.toolchain: Node >= 18, npm; tests via node --test (package.json:21, package.json:67-69)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Replace /\s*,\s*/ with split(',').map(trim) in the host getter only (or host+protocol), leaving ctx.ips on the regex.

out_of_scope_notes: Third-party deps (accepts, content-type, type-is, fresh, parseurl, cookies) parse request headers with their own regexes; not this advisory's code and not in this repo.
lib/response.js:299 and lib/request.js:111 use anchored /^https?:\/\//i tests, linear; not related.
unverified: repo_mb not measured (no shell size check); lib/ is four small files and the tree has ~108 files, so tiny_repo is inferred, not measured.
Advisory text itself was not available offline; scope taken from fix.diff History entries ('avoid redos on host and protocol getter').
Whether other copies of /\s*,\s*/ exist outside lib/ (docs, dist) was not exhaustively checked; lib/ grep shows only the three fixed sites.
